verdict.rationale: Capacities documents a block-based editor that accepts images as reusable image objects and supports embedding blocks. It also has keyboard triggers such as `((` for block references, `@`/`[[]]` for links and Cmd/Ctrl U to create objects, which supports part of the keyboard-driven, embedded-media editing story. Most named formatting elements have no evidence. Missing for 10: documented headings, callouts, tables and code blocks; evidence of embedded media beyond images; formatting-specific keyboard shortcuts or markdown syntax; hands-on corroboration of editor speed.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can write and format notes with headings, callouts, tables, code blocks, and embedded media in a fast keyboard-driven editor

citations.quote: Any image you input into Capacities becomes an image object, that can be reused anywhere in your space.
it also lets you embed individual blocks and their children inside another page.
Type `((` anywhere in your content and a search will open.
You can use `Cmd U` (Mac) or `Ctrl U` (Windows) to create a new object
